run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T22:34:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real 5xx responses served by the frontend-proxy Envoy ingress: 143.203125 STATUS_CODE_ERROR 'ingress' spans and 94.453125 'router frontend egress' error spans in 21:34:23-22:55:48 against 22299.876923 and 22352.890625 non-error spans of the same operations. The alert value 0.01111111 is consistent with a per-second error rate of about 40 errors per hour, which matches the first burst, 22:14:36-22:14:59, of HTTP 504 'UT response_timeout' returned after a 15000-15002 ms upstream timeout on GET /api/data. Sampled Jaeger traces show those /api/data requests spend essentially all their time (45.31 s, 9.07 s, 5.22 s) in the frontend client call grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, and the ad service's own flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) while flagd's server spans for the same calls complete in 86-122 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code=0. A second, larger in-window burst (22:37:08-22:43:58) consists of frontend HTTP 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout plus 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on /api/products/*, coinciding with the cart Deployment rollout at 22:36:53-22:36:56 that replaced the single cart pod (config-only change, same image). Cart itself shows no error spans and its replacement pod is ready, running with 0 restarts and serving normally. The deepest cause of the ad-to-flagd deadline-exceeded calls is not established, and the aggregated duration histograms do not corroborate the prevalence of the slow spans seen in traces.

claims.text: frontend-proxy only has two operations, 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client), and both carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in 21:34:23-22:55:48: increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total was 143.203125 for ingress and 94.453125 for router frontend egress, versus 22299.876923 and 22352.890625 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans of the same operations.

frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 504 with response flag UT response_timeout on GET /api/data (and /api/data?contextKeys=assembly|binoculars|books|travel|telescopes) with 15000-15002 ms upstream response times toward upstream 'frontend' at 100.96.3.80:8080, i.e. the 15 s Envoy upstream timeout, at 22:14:36.659Z through 22:14:59.245Z; all 20 error lines in the readable 22:14:36-22:35:13 segment fall in that 23-second burst.

Sampled frontend-proxy error traces show 'ingress' spans with error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR whose only visible child is 'router frontend egress' with error="true" and http.status_code="0" and no frontend span in the same trace (trace c40b3222b9a63859e138ddf42bd9991a: load-generator GET 503 -> frontend-proxy ingress 503 -> router frontend egress http.status_code 0 in 893138 us).

Sampled traces at 22:14-22:15 show frontend server spans 'GET /api/data' of 45318407 us, 9067597 us and 5216925 us whose slowest co-extensive child is the frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (45317485, 9066248, 5215740 us); the ad service's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans lasted 38198844 us and 7796254 us, its internal 'resolve' spans 12902166, 3095757, 2397214 and 2201314 us, and its client spans flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, while flagd's server spans flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean completed in 86 us and 122 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

frontend's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increases in the window were POST /api/cart 52.83870967741935, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 52.852459016393446, GET /api/cart 23.370967741935484, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 23.37704918032787, POST /api/checkout 18.29032258064516, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.295081967213115, tcp.connect 7.114754098360656, GET 23.370967741935484 and POST 71.12903225806451; in the same view the cart service error count was 0 and frontend-proxy ingress was 143.203125.

frontend-proxy logs for 22:36:00-22:43:58 show the frontend returning HTTP 500 ('via_upstream') for GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout from 22:37:08.410811Z to 22:37:25.934787Z, followed by HTTP 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z, /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N and /api/products/66VCHSJNUP at 22:38:10.717656Z through 22:41:29.894553Z.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo record the cart rollout: 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' at 22:36:53Z, 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0' at 22:36:56Z and 'Stopping container cart' (Killing) on Pod/cart-755465879b-rh5r4 at 22:36:56Z; both ReplicaSets are controlled by Deployment cart and use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart.

Cart's replacement pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz is Running, ready, with 0 restarts and startTime 2026-11-14T22:36:53Z; its cart container logged normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls (e.g. 22:47:23.1248604Z-22:47:31.948104Z) after the wait-for-valkey-cart init container completed, and cart's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR series read 0 at 22:44:23 and 22:54:23.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready: frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 (started 22:05:44Z, 0 restarts), frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt (22:05:45Z, 0 restarts), ad-554b849958-fbw9s (22:05:45Z, 0 restarts), flagd-77f6d5b95d-64j8j (22:07:38Z, 0 restarts, 2 ready containers) and cart-84889c965d-tkxdz; every Deployment reported desired 1, available 1, ready 1, updated 1, and fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh carried 1 restart with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled.

Over the window ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 1711.05 spans (+Inf bucket) and frontend GET /api/data had 1711.6065573770493 spans, while flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean had 0 spans recorded under service_name="ad"; the same histograms report only about 7 GET /api/data spans above the 1000 ms bucket and about 15 grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans above 1000 ms.

No traces_span_metrics samples were returned for the services queried before roughly 22:17-22:24 (first returned sample timestamps 22:19:23 and 22:24:23), so the returned metrics contain no comparable pre-burst latency baseline.

Primary explanation for the alert: frontend /api/data requests wait on the ad service (the frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds is co-extensive with the 5-45 s /api/data span), whose flagd flag-resolution calls end in gRPC status 4 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; once the request exceeds Envoy's 15 s upstream timeout the frontend-proxy returns 504 UT response_timeout, producing the ingress error spans behind the reading of 0.01111111 (about 40 errors per hour, matching the roughly 40 error lines of the 22:14:36-22:14:59 burst).

A second, larger contributor inside the same alert window: the cart Deployment rollout at 22:36:53-22:36:56 replaced the single cart pod (configuration-only change, same image), after which frontend's own grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client spans were STATUS_CODE_ERROR, frontend returned HTTP 500 for /api/cart and /api/checkout at 22:37:08-22:37:25 and connections were terminated (503 UC) for /api/products/* until 22:41:29; the fast-failure shape (cart client calls mostly sub-second) is consistent with the cart Service briefly having no serving endpoint rather than a slow cart application.

Unresolved candidate: most otel-demo pods were created at 22:05:43-22:05:46 and flagd at 22:07:38, roughly seven minutes before the first error burst, and ad, fraud-detection and recommendation also carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (2.042553191489362, 2.03921568627451 and 4.065573770491803 in the window); a flagd-related disruption around that replacement could explain why ad's flag-resolution calls hit client deadlines, but no returned evidence ties that replacement to this cause.

Rejected: flagd itself being slow or failing. In the supplied trace flagd's server spans flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean completed in 86 us and 122 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 at the same times as the ad client spans that timed out, and the flagd pod was running, ready and un-restarted.

Rejected as far as the evidence goes: a failing cart application or cart datastore. Cart's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR series read 0, the cart Deployment reported 1 of 1 available and ready replicas, the replacement pod had 0 restarts and its wait-for-valkey-cart init container completed, and its cart container served GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync normally; the frontend's cart errors are its own client-side RPC errors during the pod replacement.

The aggregated duration histograms do not corroborate the slow-ad story quantitatively: for ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds the +Inf bucket equals the le="1000.0" bucket (1711.05), i.e. no span above 1 s, and for frontend GET /api/data the le="15000.0" bucket equals +Inf (1711.6065573770493) with only about 7 spans above 1 s, even though sampled Jaeger spans show a 38.2 s GetAds and a 45.3 s GET /api/data at 22:14-22:15; the prevalence of the slow calls is therefore unknown even though the individual slow spans are attested by traces.

Checked and not affected: flagd (pod running, ready, 0 restarts; its server spans sub-millisecond with rpc.grpc.status_code=0) and the cart service (0 error spans, 1/1 available replicas, replacement pod ready with 0 restarts and normal request logs). The frontend and frontend-proxy pods were also running with 0 restarts, so pod state is not the fault; their failure appears only in their own error spans, 5xx logs and latency.

Investigate why ad's flagd gRPC client calls reach DEADLINE_EXCEEDED while flagd's handler answers in microseconds: inspect ad's flagd client deadline, resolver/keepalive settings and the flagd Service endpoints (flagd exposes ports 8013, 8016 and 4000) during 22:14-22:16, comparing with the flagd pod replacement at 22:07:38.

Remove rollout-induced cart unavailability: cart runs as a single replica, and its 22:36:53-22:36:56 replacement left frontend's cart and checkout calls failing (HTTP 500) and connections terminated until 22:41:29; a rollout strategy of maxUnavailable 0 or more than one cart replica would eliminate this second error source.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data and a type=alert listing returned no_data, so the alert expression, threshold window and error-ratio denominator could not be verified.

Kubernetes state metrics are absent from this Prometheus target: get_metric_names {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned no_data and get_series for kube_pod_container_info returned no_data, so pod/ReplicaSet history could not be shown; Pod and ReplicaSet facts come from the Kubernetes API at query time only and cannot prove earlier state.

flagd logs could not be read (0 lines read for containers init-config, flagd and flagd-ui, status no_data), and the ad log scan for error|deadline|exceed|fail|warn read 3492 lines with no match and status no_data, so the reason ad's flagd calls hit DEADLINE_EXCEEDED is unknown.
Jaeger held data only up to about 22:15-22:22 in the queried window, so the 22:37-22:44 error burst has no trace-level attribution; its evidence is metrics plus frontend-proxy access logs.

frontend container logs were unreadable for 22:20-22:55 (both log fetches returned no_data with 0 lines read), so frontend's own error strings for the /api/data timeouts and the cart/checkout 500s are unknown.

The cause of the cart Deployment pod-template change at 22:36:53Z, and of the namespace-wide pod replacement at 22:05:43-22:07:38, is unknown: the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run and no actor appears in the events.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh holds 1 restart with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, but its termination time could not be established and no evidence ties it to frontend-proxy's errors, so it is an unexplained change in the window rather than observed impact.

Prevalence of the slow ad/frontend calls is uncertain because the aggregated duration histograms contradict the sampled slow spans, and no pre-burst latency baseline was returned (first samples around 22:17-22:24).
next_steps: Query the Alertmanager/Prometheus source that owns the RequestErrorRate rule to confirm its error-ratio expression and evaluation window.
Review ad's flagd client configuration (deadline, resolver, keepalive) and flagd Service endpoints for 22:14-22:16, and re-check flagd logs when log retention permits.
Review change history / CI-CD audit for who or what changed the cart pod template at 22:36:53Z and whether it was an automatic response to the earlier errors.
Retrieve frontend application logs for 22:10-22:45 from a system that retains them to confirm the exact errors raised by the /api/data route and by the cart gRPC calls.
